rounds.text: Lime Chemicals Ltd is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround that is not yet reflected in the broader market sentiment. The company has achieved a remarkable 56% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E17] and a 2700% increase in compounded profit growth [E18], signaling a sharp departure from its historical performance. This momentum is supported by a consistent improvement in margins, with the quarterly operating margin rising by 18 percentage points year-over-year [E26] and a trend of increasing operating margins over the last five quarters [E28]. Management is actively strengthening the balance sheet by reducing borrowings from Rs 4.78 Cr to Rs 3.76 Cr [E33], [E45], while simultaneously generating positive free cash flow of Rs 0.51 Cr [E31]. Furthermore, the commitment from leadership is evident as promoters have increased their stake to 30.43% [E35]. Conceded: the company faces challenges with a high P/E ratio [E6], [E60], a negative 10-year sales growth trend [E14], and a low return on equity [E13], [E49].

Lime Chemicals Ltd currently trades at a significant premium to its sector, with a P/E of 32.49x compared to the 19.24x benchmark and an EV/EBITDA of 34.22x against a 10.49x sector average [E6, E11]. This valuation is difficult to justify given the company’s long-term track record of declining sales, which have compounded at -13% over the last decade and -23% over the last three years [E14, E16]. The stock is fundamentally expensive, as evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 4.08x against a sector benchmark of 1.76x and a discounted cash flow analysis suggesting the stock is overvalued by 44.3% [E7, E39, E40]. Furthermore, the company carries substantial leverage with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.77x, and it faces potential financial strain from contingent liabilities amounting to Rs 4.94 Cr [E32, E50]. Institutional confidence appears to have evaporated, as foreign institutional holdings have dropped from 7.38% to 0.00% since December 2023 [E36]. Conceded: the company has shown recent improvement in operating margins and a significant increase in trailing twelve-month profit growth [E25, E26, E18]. Nevertheless, the current market price assumes an aggressive 15% earnings growth rate that exceeds the base case expectation, leaving little room for error in a business that has historically struggled with negative returns on equity [E41, E13, E23].

The bear’s reliance on historical sales growth [E14, E16] ignores the clear evidence of a structural turnaround, as evidenced by the 56% compounded sales growth in the trailing twelve months [E17]. While the bear highlights high valuation multiples [E6, E11], it fails to account for the fact that the company is currently outperforming expectations, with profit growth exceeding price growth by 2707% [E43]. Conceded: the company has a high debt-to-equity ratio of 1.77x [E32] and significant contingent liabilities [E50]. However, the bear overlooks that management is actively addressing this, having successfully reduced borrowings from Rs 4.78 Cr to Rs 3.76 Cr in the last year [E33, E45]. Furthermore, the claim that institutional confidence has evaporated ignores the fact that promoters have demonstrated their own conviction by increasing their stake from 29.27% to 30.43% [E35]. Finally, the bear’s focus on past negative returns [E13, E23] is contradicted by the most recent data, which shows a consistent five-quarter trend of increasing operating margins [E28] and a strong positive free cash flow of Rs 0.51 Cr [E31].

The bull’s reliance on recent sales growth [E17] ignores the long-term reality of a business that has suffered compounded sales declines of 13%, 20%, and 23% over the last ten, five, and three years respectively [E14, E15, E16]. While the bull points to profit growth [E43], this is a volatile metric that follows a period of negative returns, as evidenced by a three-year median ROE of -8% and a one-year ROE of -9% [E23, E24]. Conceded: the company has reduced debt [E33, E45]. However, this reduction does not negate the fact that debt still exceeds net worth with a 1.77x debt-to-equity ratio [E32], nor does it address the significant risk posed by Rs 4.94 Cr in contingent liabilities [E50]. The bull cites promoter stake increases [E35] as a sign of conviction, yet this ignores the total exit of foreign institutional investors, who dropped their holding from 7.38% to 0.00% [E36]. Finally, the current valuation remains detached from fundamentals, as the stock trades at a P/E of 33.3x [E1] and a P/B of 4.08x [E2], both of which significantly exceed sector benchmarks [E6, E7].
